title: University of Houston-Clear Lake (UH)
summary: University of Houston-Clear Lake (UH) is a university in Houston. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with UH.

sections.heading: What UH is known for
paragraphs: The University of Houston-Clear Lake (UH) is a public institution known for its diverse academic offerings and accessible admission process, with an admission rate of approximately 90.5%. The university serves an undergraduate population of 6,078 students, reflecting its role as a significant educational provider in the region. UH is particularly recognized for its strong business programs, which constitute about 21.8% of its academic offerings. Additionally, health-related programs make up nearly 4.8% of the curriculum, highlighting the university's commitment to fields that address community and societal needs. These characteristics underscore UH's focus on providing practical and career-oriented education within a public university framework.

sections.heading: Undergraduate admissions
paragraphs: Undergraduate admissions at the University of Houston-Clear Lake (UH) are characterized by an admission rate of approximately 90.52%, indicating a relatively open acceptance policy. The average SAT score for admitted students is 1060, reflecting the academic profile of the incoming class. UH does not currently utilize the Common Application or offer an early decision option for undergraduate admissions. Prospective students can expect a straightforward admissions process with these criteria in mind.

sections.heading: How to read UH tuition
paragraphs: The University of Houston-Clear Lake (UH) tuition varies depending on residency status. In-state students pay $7,770 for tuition, while out-of-state students are charged $21,114. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition, fees, and other expenses, amounts to $24,622. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and their families plan financially for their education at UH.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: The University of Houston-Clear Lake (UH) offers financial aid to support students in managing the cost of their education. Approximately 45.24% of UH students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies for low-income students. For those who complete their programs, the median debt is $17,831, reflecting the typical amount borrowed to finance their studies. Prospective students can explore detailed cost and aid information through UH's official website at www.uhcl.edu/ or consult the College Scorecard page at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?225414 for additional financial data.

The median debt for students who complete their degrees is $17,831, providing insight into the typical financial burden carried by graduates.
